issues.detail: The Greek 'η σεβασμα' (the worshipful/reverent one) is translated as 'đối tượng thờ phượng' (object of worship). In this context, it refers to the entity being worshipped/honored as a deity, but the Vietnamese rendering shifts the focus slightly from the status of the entity to its role as an object.

The Greek 'ωστε' (so that/in order that) expresses purpose or result. The Vietnamese 'đến nỗi' (to the extent that/so that) captures the result, but the phrase 'αυτον εις τον ναον του θεου ως θεον καθισαι' implies the act of *seating* himself as God in the temple. The Vietnamese 'ngồi trong đền thờ' (sits in the temple) misses the specific nuance of 'καθισαι' (taking a seat/establishing oneself as) as a formal action of enthronement.
